tip: yerine follows the noun to mean instead of it: restoran yerine = instead of a restaurant.
The -abilir slice adds can or may: kullanabilir = can use, from kullan plus abilir.
To turn an adjective into a yes/no question, add the particle after it: boş mu = is it empty.
The -e ending marks a destination: hastaneye = to the hospital, from hastane plus ye.
To finish doing something, the action takes -meyi before bitirdi: pişirmeyi bitirdi = finished cooking.
The -tan ending means from: mutfaktan = from the kitchen, from mutfak plus tan.
The from and to pair uses -ten then -e: çiçekten çiçeğe = from flower to flower.
The -yı ending marks a specific, definite object: baklavayı = the baklava, a known particular one.
var means there is and sits at the end, with the place in the -da form: Kutuda ... var = there is in the box.
The -müş ending marks hearsay or a fresh realization: bugünmüş = apparently it is today.
A proper name takes an apostrophe before any suffix: Beyoğlu'nda = in Beyoğlu.
The -ken ending means when or while: Küçükken = when I was little.
Between X and Y is X ile Y arasında, with arasında last: Park ile okul arasında = between the park and the school.
The -arak ending turns a verb into by doing it: koşarak çıktım = I went out running.
After a base verb, için means in order to: gitmek için = in order to go.
The -il slice makes a verb passive: yıkılacak = will be demolished, with no doer named.
After kaç meaning how many, the noun stays singular: kaç fosil, never kaç fosiller.
